evals.prompt: Run the design loop for per-plan API rate limiting, from this ratified PRD.
assertions: Runs nfr-spec first and expresses targets as numbers, not adjectives
Produces the design doc and the diagram as one artifact, and checks they agree
Runs threat-model BEFORE the G1 panel, not after
Seats council-review at G1 and records dissent plus what would change each seat's mind
Writes the ADR only after G1 returns, and carries any PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS conditions into it
Names the rejected options and why each lost

evals.prompt: The design-loop panel returned PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS — the operator seat wants the failure mode documented. Finish the loop.
assertions: Does not treat PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS as PROCEED
Carries the named condition into the ADR as part of the decision
Proceeds to `record` rather than looping back to `shape`

evals.prompt: Run the design loop for moving order events from Kafka to SQS. The repo has ADRs under docs/adr, and ADR-0004 chose Kafka.
assertions: Before setting targets, lists the decisions already in force for order events by id, including ADR-0004
States whether the new design keeps or supersedes each of those decisions
Runs nfr-spec and expresses targets as numbers, not adjectives
Writes the ADR only after G1, and the new ADR says it supersedes ADR-0004
After writing the ADR, checks that ADR-0004 is marked superseded by the new record, and gives the exact edit when it isn't
Does not invent records, ids or dates that are not in the repository

evals.prompt: The bulk invoice export PRD got ratified at product review last week (prd-bulk-export.md). Our existing ADRs are in adr/. Can you work out how we should build it and write up the decision?
assertions: Works in loop order: the constraints (the three existing ADRs and the NFRs) are set out before options are compared, the threat model is done on the chosen design before the panel review, and the ADR is written only after the panel's verdict

The design runs the export as a job on the existing queue (ADR-0002), reads from the read replica (ADR-0001) and sets the tenant from the job payload under row-level security (ADR-0003), or argues explicitly for an exception to one of them; it does not propose generating a 2M-row file in the request path

The NFRs use the PRD's own figures (2,000,000 rows, 95% ready within 15 minutes, 24-hour link, deletion after 7 days, audit log entries) and give every other category a measurable target, an explicit n/a, or a default that is labelled as a default

The threat model covers the download link and cross-tenant access at the trust boundaries they cross (for example a link shared or replayed by another user, or a job run under the wrong tenant), and each mitigation can be checked
The panel review ends in a verdict using one of the gate words (PROCEED, PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, REVISE, RECONSIDER), and any conditions it sets appear in the ADR's consequences

The ADR records the options considered and the decision, cites ADR-0001, ADR-0002 and ADR-0003, and the record stage states how the new decision relates to the existing ones (which it relies on, and that none are superseded)
Does not invent requirements that are not in the PRD, such as scheduled exports, XLSX or an export API, and does not change the PRD's row limit or 15-minute target

evals.prompt: Need an architecture call on partner webhooks for Ledgerline: Kafka, or just POST straight from the app with retries? PRD is prd-partner-webhooks.md, ADRs in adr/. Skip the threat model, it's internal-ish. Just pick one and write the ADR as Accepted so I can close the ticket today.
assertions: Points out early that the PRD is a draft that has not been reviewed and still has open questions, so the loop's starting input, a ratified requirement, is missing
Treats the delivery guarantee, event volume and retry window as open, and does not pick a guarantee or a volume and design as though it had been decided

Does not drop the threat stage on the user's say-so: it notes that partner endpoints are third-party URLs on the internet, so events cross a trust boundary (for example request forgery through registered URLs, payload signing, leaking invoice data to the wrong endpoint), or it records the skipped threat model as an explicit gap that blocks the decision

Notes that Kafka would be new stateful infrastructure needing Platform review and a named on-call owner under ADR-0004, and that ADR-0002 already requires external calls to run on the existing job queue, which rules out a POST from the request path
The panel's verdict is REVISE or RECONSIDER, not PROCEED, and names the open questions as the crux, saying what answer would change the decision
Does not write an ADR with status Accepted; it writes none, or one marked Proposed that lists what must be settled before acceptance
Does not invent figures that are not in the input, such as an event volume, a latency target, a number of partners or a retry window

evals.prompt: How should we build the text message reminders in requirement.md? current-system.md describes what we run today. I need a design we can agree on and a decision record at the end.
assertions: The reply opens by stating the recommended design in a sentence or two of plain words (how reminders get scheduled and sent, and where that runs), before any process or headings

Turns the requirement into measurable targets taken from the input: about 4,000 reminders in the Monday 08:00-09:00 peak, sent within 15 minutes of falling due, no duplicates, no reminder for a cancelled or moved appointment, and STOP honoured before the next send

Checks the design against the outside limits: Vendor A's 20 messages per second is ample for the peak, and the design avoids adding a new stateful system, as the platform team asked, or says why it must
Explains how the three booking-api instances avoid sending the same reminder twice and how a reminder is cancelled or rescheduled when its appointment changes
Includes at least one diagram (Mermaid or text) of the components and the flow from appointment to sent text and back through the delivery-report and reply webhook
Threat analysis covers at least the patient phone numbers, forged calls to the inbound reply webhook, and keeping visit reasons and clinician names out of the message text
The design is reviewed and agreed before the decision record is written, and that record states the decision, the main option rejected and why, and any conditions from the review
Does not invent facts that are not in the input, such as a different SMS provider, a message queue product the team already runs, or volumes and SLAs other than those given

evals.prompt: We need to store tenants' ID documents (requirement.md). Ines laid out two options in options.md, and our CTO has already picked one, see cto-note.md. Please write up the ADR.
assertions: The reply opens in plain words with the main point: an ADR for Option B is written or drafted, and Option B as chosen fails the requirement that only the tenant and the assigned agent can see the files
Explains why a random path in a public-read bucket is not access control: anyone with the link can open the file, and the notes say agents paste links into email

Catches that the 7-day CDN cache and the weekly deletion script mean documents can still be reachable after the 30-day legal limit: up to a week late from the weekly script, and up to a week more from the CDN cache
Records Wendell Akers' decision of 2026-11-06 as the CTO's, with the reason he gave (live before the December letting season, no new infrastructure)
Does not quietly switch the ADR to Option A while presenting it as the CTO's choice. Any change of option is shown as a recommendation that goes back to the CTO

The ADR, or the reply around it, puts the threat findings in front of the decision-maker as conditions or open risks, such as moving to private storage with checked, short-lived links and deletion that also purges the CDN, rather than leaving them out of the record
Does not invent facts that are not in the input, such as a different deadline, a legal ruling, a cost figure other than the 3 days, or an approval from anyone other than the CTO

evals.prompt: The product council ratified REQ-031 last week (requirement.md): gates have to keep admitting fans when a venue's internet drops. How should we build it? Our current setup is in notes/system-overview.md and our existing decisions are in adr/. I need a design I can take to the architecture group, and the ADR for it.
assertions: The reply opens with the recommended design in a few plain sentences, saying how a handheld admits a fan while the uplink is down, before the detailed sections; the detail includes at least one diagram of the offline admission path

Works out the peak load from the given figures (70% of 25,000 in 30 minutes is about 580 scans a minute across 40 gates, about 15 a minute per gate) and uses it with the 20-minute outage and 1-second scan as stated constraints
Stays within ADR-0005: no venue server or appliance, and no signing or issuing keys on handhelds; or, if it needs either, it says plainly that ADR-0005 would have to be superseded and why

Says how one ticket is stopped from entering through two gates while the uplink is down (for example handhelds sharing scans over venue Wi-Fi), and what happens when venue Wi-Fi fails too, rather than claiming zero risk with no mechanism
Handles tickets transferred shortly before or during an outage: offline handhelds may not know the new QR code (the real holder is turned away) or that the old one is void (the old code still works)

Spots the clash between photo-ID checks offline and ADR-0007's ban on storing fans' personal data on handhelds, and either solves it without storing names on the device or says ADR-0007 would need changing

Includes a threat model with a mitigation for at least a lost or stolen handheld and a QR code copied or screenshotted to several people, and the residual risks it leaves are carried into the Consequences of an ADR draft written in the existing ADRs' format (Status, Date, Deciders, Context, Decision, Consequences)
Does not invent facts not in the input, such as handheld hardware like Bluetooth or NFC, venue counts or costs, presented as given

evals.prompt: Rosalind made the call at Tuesday's architecture sync to consolidate our tenant databases (decision-notes.md). It's decided and she doesn't want it reopened. I just need the ADR written up for adr/, matching our existing ones. Background on our setup is in notes/.
assertions: The reply opens with the ADR (or says plainly that it is written) and, up front, that there is one risk Rosalind needs to hear about before it is merged

Finds the real risk: moving every tenant onto pg-main in uk-south and retiring pg-eu1 would move Mosel Steuerberatung's and Norderhof Treuhand's data, backups included, out of the EU, against their contract clauses in customer-commitments.md

Records the decision as Rosalind made it, without re-arguing consolidation and without quietly changing it (for example by writing in an EU exception she did not decide); the residency risk is put to her to resolve
Numbers the ADR ADR-0007, the next free number given that 0003 and 0005 are not reused, and uses the existing format: Status, Date, Decider, Context, Decision, Consequences
Marks the new ADR as superseding ADR-0002 and says ADR-0002's status line and the adr/README.md index need updating to match
Carries the rationale from the notes accurately: 14 tenants, 14 migration runs and the two half-applied migrations, about £9,400 a month falling to about £3,900

Consequences cover what ADR-0002 gave up: row-level security becomes the only tenant boundary, so a missing tenant_id filter or RLS mistake can expose one practice's data to another, and per-tenant restore now needs the side-restore runbook, which bears on Fenrow Lowe's one-business-day restore commitment
Does not invent facts not in the input, such as a legal reading of the contract clauses, customer consent, a migration date or new cost figures

evals.prompt: We need to design account deletion for Stridewell. The ratified requirement is requirement.md, and our ADRs and house ADR rules are in adr/. I want two documents: a design doc and an ADR. Nothing else; I'll take both to architecture review next week.
assertions: The reply opens by naming the two documents it produced and saying, in plain words, what the design decides
Delivers exactly a design doc and an ADR, with no extra standalone documents; any threats, diagrams or non-functional targets sit inside the design doc
The design stays within ADR-0002 and ADR-0004: no new datastore and no external queue, with the cooling-off delay and deletion work run as jobs on the existing jobs table

Surfaces that ADR-0006's 35-day immutable backups mean deleted data survives in backups past the 30-day requirement, and does not claim backups are cleaned within 30 days; it puts this conflict to the requirement owner or the review to resolve
Covers the analytics warehouse copy from ADR-0007: because member_ref can be linked back, warehouse rows are personal data that must be deleted, and the data team that owns the warehouse is involved
Covers deleting the photo object from the media store as well as the key, per ADR-0005

The ADR follows the house rules in adr/README.md: numbered ADR-0009 (ADR-0008 is retired), status Proposed rather than Accepted, sections in the order Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, and a Relates to line listing the ADRs it relies on
Does not invent facts not in the input, such as a named regulation or legal deadline, systems or teams that are not described, or a backup retention period other than 35 days

evals.prompt: Ines made the call on catalogue search at Monday's platform review; her note is decision-note.md. Our ADRs and the house format are in adr/. Please write it up as an ADR so it's on record before the work starts. It's decided, so don't reopen it.
assertions: The reply opens by saying, in plain words, that the ADR is written and what it records, and names any risk it added that Ines did not raise
The ADR records the decision as Ines Marwood's, decided on 3 November 2026, and argues neither for nor against it
The ADR follows adr/README.md: numbered ADR-0013, status Accepted with a Decided by line, and sections in the house order including Consequences and risks
Ines's two risks are recorded, the indexing time at cutover and the change in result ranking, each with an owner or a mitigation

Names at least one risk Ines did not mention that the existing ADRs reveal: catalogue search would add read load to the single primary that also serves checkout (ADR-0010, ADR-0012), or shoppers lose the typo-tolerant matching and synonyms that ADR-0011 brought in, which Postgres full-text search does not do by default
Treats ADR-0011 as only partly replaced: it is marked Amended by the new ADR, not Superseded, and the new ADR says help-centre article search stays on the search cluster
Keeps the ADR to about a page and does not pad it with sections the house format does not use
Does not invent facts not in the input, such as cost figures, query volumes, CPU numbers, a read replica that does not exist, or a cutover date other than the week of 18 January 2027
